# Spiritual Translation: The Five Purgations of the Natural Mind

---

### Structural Note

The chapter describes a single process occurring through five distinct faculties of the natural mind. In each case, an obscure mixed state — containing both genuine spiritual life and dominant evil affections entangled together — is elevated toward the Divine Affection for Truth. She attracts, separates, and purifies. The evil affections, once stripped of their covering, wreak destruction *characteristic of their faculty of origin* before divine truths finally bind them:

| Faculty | Evil stripped produces | Correspondence |
|---|---|---|
| Love (fire) | Burning, consuming | Self-love devours every state it touches |
| Truth (water) | Frost, hail, snow | Absence of love freezes and shatters interior truths, works, and perceptions |
| Thought (wind) | Storms, waves, shipwreck | Intellectual violence agitates doctrine and memory, destroys frameworks of teaching |
| Wisdom (light) | *(stripped in stillness)* | Evil from perverted wisdom acts more subtly |
| General understanding (air) | Mixed, quiet destruction | Commingled falsity corrupts whatever it finds |

The entirety is a teaching on regeneration through temptation: the purgation of each faculty of the mind, the spiritual combat that attends it, and the final confinement of evil in the outermost states of the natural memory — the seven abysses beyond the sphere where spiritual life operates.

So, the cloud shall ascend from fire to the heavens towards the likeness of the Virgin of Light that she shall display to it. Its sign is the flashes that occur with lightning storms [ ... i]ts exchange [ ... ]. And they shall be purified by her towards [ ... ] the light that she shall reveal [to them]. The rulers shall be released by the lightning storms and they are freed and sent.

However, [these] angels shall immediately be summoned to them, so that they will seize them, because they know that they shall never do good. Every place they will touch they shall make dead and a loss. Whenever the angels will make towards them and come beside [them], they shall flee in their constraint before them. They go into whatever they will meet upon and assume it, like a robber being abandoned and fleeing before one stronger than him, as he runs after him to arrest him.

Now, those rulers that shall be freed from these clouds and assume whatever they will meet upon [and enter] into the [ ... / ... ] that they did not [choose] will seize this thing, whether indeed a tree to which they have found the way, or animals, or people. Simply, every place that they will assume they shall burn and destroy by the fire of their body. Namely, the rulers, [the] children of fire, they that shall be stripped of the fire.

In contrast, [the] cloud that shall be raised up from water, and comes above towards the Virgin of Light; its sign is the thunder storms and the booms that shall come in the atmosphere in various forms and are heard. fills.explanation: The phrase "come above" is used repeatedly in the Kephalaia for clouds ascending toward the Virgin (¶6: "comes above towards the Virgin of Light"; ¶12: "comes above towards the image of the Virgin"), describing the progressive ascent from the earth to the intermediate atmospheric region.
Following the pattern in ¶3 where the Virgin "shall display to it," the light she reveals is directed to the lives being purified; "to them" indicates the recipients of the revealed light.
The demonstrative "these" correctly introduces the angels summoned in response to the released rulers, matching the proximate reference to the angels described throughout the chapter.
The angels come beside the rulers (them), prompting the rulers to flee; the pronoun "them" refers to the rulers, the direct object of the angels' pursuit.

The rulers assume whatever form they encounter and then enter into a place/body they did not choose; "and enter" bridges the two coordinate actions of seizing a form and inhabiting it, consistent with the robber metaphor of ¶4.
The robber metaphor in ¶4 establishes that rulers flee and grab whatever is available, not what they would choose; "did not choose" conveys their indiscriminate seizure of any available form.
The definite article "the" before "children of fire" is grammatically required and correctly identifies the rulers as the specific offspring of fire.
The definite article "the" before "cloud" is required to introduce the specific water cloud as the second of the five clouds described.

fills.fill: And the lives in it shall be purified.
fills.explanation: Every cloud section follows the pattern: sign described → lives purified → rulers stripped; paralleling ¶10 ("the lives be purified"), ¶11 ("The lives in it shall be cleansed"), and ¶12 ("the lives are purified in it"), the water cloud section requires its purification statement here.
The preposition and article "in a" correctly introduces the water cloud as the constraining environment from which the rulers flee, matching the natural syntax.
The pronoun "they" refers back to the water-rulers just described, introducing their destructive actions in parallel with the fire-rulers of ¶4-5.

The verb "reach" is the consistent term used throughout the chapter for rulers arriving at and affecting a place (¶4: "every place they will touch"; ¶7: "every place they will reach"; ¶12: "every place they will find").

After listing specific damages (frost, hail, snow, ruined seed-corn, fruits, plants), a summarizing verb of total destruction is needed for "every place they reach," paralleling ¶5's "burn and destroy."
The relative pronoun "that" connects "every place" to the relative clause "they will reach," a construction used identically throughout the chapter.
The wind-rulers produce characteristic destruction in rivers and seas; "tempests" pairs naturally with "waves" and matches the wind cloud's vocabulary (¶10: "winds and tempests").
Waves and tempests characteristically overturn ships at sea; "overturn" captures the violent action of wind-rulers on doctrinal frameworks (ships) in both natural and correspondential senses.
The destruction is wrought "in them" — referring to the rivers and seas just mentioned as the domain where the wind-rulers operate.
Wind-rulers seize and bring ships/people to the deep, completing the maritime destruction sequence of waves, tempests, overturning, and drowning in the depths.
Following the pattern in ¶3 where the Virgin "shall display to it" (the cloud), she likewise displays the sign of the light cloud to it.
The rulers come forth "from it" (the light cloud), paralleling ¶10 "they descend from it" and ¶12 "come from it" — the standard expression for rulers departing their cloud.

The temporal conjunction "until" introduces the resolution of each cloud section where angels finally seize the rulers, matching the recurring pattern of rulers wreaking destruction until angelic intervention.

Confirming the editor's choice; while other sections use "the likeness," the variation to "the image" for the fifth cloud (mingled air) is consistent with the text's pattern of varied formulations (¶6 uses neither term), and the spiritual reading's "the form" supports either term.

Every cloud section describes "the lives" being purified or cleansed (¶10: "the lives be purified"; ¶11: "The lives in it shall be cleansed"); "the lives" is the consistent subject of purification throughout.

The transitional formula "Again, the/these rulers" consistently introduces the stripping of rulers after the purification of lives (¶10: "Again, the rulers will be stripped"; ¶11: "Again, the rulers that will be stripped"), making this the required bridge from "rest" to "these rulers."

The "ditches and the depths" form a natural cosmological pairing describing the seven outer states of confinement in the great sea, extending downward until they reach the lowest earths at the feet of the Porter.
The prepositional phrase "to the feet of the Porter" completes the description of how deep the ditches reach — down to the feet/foundation of the Porter (Guardian of the ultimate boundary).

The text immediately following mentions "this offspring... tree and that of flesh," and ¶5 establishes tree and flesh (animals/people) as the two categories rulers assume; "the tree" completes the pair with "the flesh."

Angels set a "watch" (sentinel/guard) over the rulers confined in tree and flesh to guard them until the appointed time of stripping — a standard term for divine oversight constraining evil until its appointed removal.
The rulers are gathered "together" above after being stripped from tree and flesh, describing their collective assembly for final processing — extraction of remaining light and casting down.

The rulers are "poured out and cast" into their original forms, using metallurgical imagery of molten material being poured and cast into molds, restoring them to their first shapes before the final extraction of light.

The partial word gap bridges "for[ms]" and "[im]ages" — "forms and images" is the standard doublet in the Kephalaia for the complete essential shape of spiritual beings, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "forms and essential states."
The text explicitly states these rulers are cast to "the place to where these former ones were cast"; "also" marks the parallel fate of this second group reaching the same confinement as the first.
